library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Shortal_2018_propofol_mouse"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Shortal_2018_propofol_mouse"))$description`
* Article (open access): <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0194949>
* Authors' MATLAB TCI code: <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.1205136>

Shortal et al. (2018) infused propofol through a jugular catheter in adult
male C57BL/6 mice and measured propofol by HPLC in serial cortical brain
biopsies and in blood. A linear three-compartment model (Eq 1; Fig 1C) was
fitted to all four infusion paradigms at once: compartment 1 is blood,
compartment 2 is brain and compartment 3 lumps every other tissue. Drug enters
and leaves only through blood. The fitted model then drove a brain
target-controlled infusion (TCI) adapted from the STANPUMP algorithm, which
was validated prospectively at brain targets of 10 and 15 ug/g.

# Population

The model was fitted to 241 samples (193 brain, 48 blood) from 21 adult male
C57BL/6 mice aged 2.90 +/- 0.45 months and weighing 27.4 +/- 1.5 g (Methods,
'Animals' and 'Surgery'). The four paradigms were a 15 mg/kg bolus given as
150 mg/kg/min for 6 s (n = 4), a 2 mg/kg/min infusion for 1 h (n = 4), and two
generations of TCI targeting 10 ug/g brain (n = 5 and n = 8; Results, Figs 3
and 4). A further 10 mice (68 brain, 12 blood samples) were used only for
validation (Fig 5). The mice were under isoflurane for surgery, reduced to a
sub-anaesthetic 0.2 percent during propofol infusion.

```{r population}
str(rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Shortal_2018_propofol_mouse"))$population)
```

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lk_central_brain` (paper `k12`, blood to brain) | log(1.55) 1/min | Table 1 |
| `lk_brain_central` (paper `k21`, brain to blood) | log(2.71) 1/min | Table 1 |
| `lk12` (paper `k13`, blood to other tissues) | log(0.22) 1/min | Table 1 |
| `lk21` (paper `k31`, other tissues to blood) | log(0.04) 1/min | Table 1 |
| `lkel` (paper `k10`, elimination from blood) | log(0.07) 1/min | Table 1 |
| `lvc` (paper `sinf`, blood volume per kg) | log(0.35) L/kg | Table 1; Methods 'Three compartment model' |
| `addSd`, `addSd_Cbrain` | fixed(0) | Methods 'Fitting procedure' (unweighted least squares; no residual variance reported) |
| `d/dt(central)`, `d/dt(brain)`, `d/dt(peripheral1)` | n/a | Eq 1 (multiplied through by `vc = sinf * WT`) |
| Input `I(t) / sinf` | n/a | Eq 1; `kInf * I(t)` in `TCIMaster2.m` of the authors' code |
| `Cc = central / vc`, `Cbrain = brain / vc` | n/a | Eq 1 (`x1`, `x2` are the blood and brain concentrations) |

The authors' code (`TCIMaster2.m`) carries the final constants in 1/s as
`k = [0.0258 0.0452 0.0037 0.0007 0.0012 2.8373]` for `[k12 k21 k13 k31 k10 kInf]`.
Converted to 1/min these are 1.548, 2.712, 0.222, 0.042 and 0.072, and
`1 / kInf = 0.352` L/kg; Table 1 is the same set rounded to two decimals. The
packaged model uses the published Table 1 values.

```{r code-vs-table}
code_k <- c(k12 = 0.0258, k21 = 0.0452, k13 = 0.0037, k31 = 0.0007, k10 = 0.0012) * 60
table_k <- c(k12 = 1.55, k21 = 2.71, k13 = 0.22, k31 = 0.04, k10 = 0.07)
cmp_k <- tibble::tibble(
  constant = names(table_k),
  table_1 = table_k,
  code_per_min = code_k[names(table_k)]
)
knitr::kable(cmp_k, digits = 3, caption = "Table 1 vs the authors' code (1/min).")
# Table 1 is the code's constant set rounded to 2 decimals.
stopifnot(all(abs(cmp_k$table_1 - cmp_k$code_per_min) <= 0.005 + 1e-9))
stopifnot(abs(0.35 - 1 / 2.8373) <= 0.005)
```

# Simulation helpers

The model has no between-animal or residual variability, so every simulation
below is the typical-value prediction for one mouse. Infusion rates are given
by the paper in mg/kg/min; the event tables convert them to mg/min with the
mouse's weight, which then cancels against `vc = sinf * WT`.

The model declares two endpoints (blood `Cc` and brain `Cbrain`), so every
observation row carries `dvid = 1`; the solve returns both concentrations as
columns on every row.

```{r helpers}
mod <- readModelDb("Shortal_2018_propofol_mouse")
wt <- 0.0274 # kg, mean body weight of the study mice

# One subject; infusions in mg/kg/min with durations in min.
make_events <- function(start, rate_mgkgmin, dur, obs_times, wt = 0.0274) {
  doses <- tibble::tibble(
    id = 1L, time = start, evid = 1L, cmt = "central",
    amt = rate_mgkgmin * dur * wt, rate = rate_mgkgmin * wt, dvid = NA_integer_
  )
  obs <- tibble::tibble(
    id = 1L, time = obs_times, evid = 0L, cmt = NA_character_,
    amt = 0, rate = 0, dvid = 1L
  )
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(WT = wt)
}

solve_typical <- function(events) {
  # A one-subject solve returns no `id` column; add it back for PKNCA.
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    dplyr::mutate(id = 1L, .before = 1)
}
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figures 3A/4A and 3B/4B: bolus and fixed-rate infusion

Figure 3A/4A starts the 6 s bolus (150 mg/kg/min) at 5 min; Figure 3B/4B runs
2 mg/kg/min from 5 to 65 min. The thick lines in those figures are the final
model's predictions.

```{r figs-3-4}
obs_a <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 60, by = 0.02))))
sim_a <- solve_typical(make_events(5, 150, 0.1, obs_a)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(paradigm = "A: 15 mg/kg bolus (150 mg/kg/min x 6 s)")
obs_b <- seq(0, 170, by = 0.25)
sim_b <- solve_typical(make_events(5, 2, 60, obs_b)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(paradigm = "B: 2 mg/kg/min x 60 min")

dplyr::bind_rows(sim_a, sim_b) |>
  dplyr::select(paradigm, time, Blood = Cc, Brain = Cbrain) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Blood, Brain), names_to = "matrix", values_to = "conc") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, conc, colour = matrix)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~paradigm, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Blood = "darkred", Brain = "black")) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (min)", y = "Propofol concentration (ug/mL blood, ug/g brain)",
    colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates the model lines of Figures 3A, 3B, 4A and 4B of Shortal 2018."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

The values read off the published model lines are compared below with the
packaged model. The figure values were read by the maintainers from the
published raster figures, so agreement within about 10 percent is the most
that can be expected.

```{r figs-3-4-check}
peak_a_blood <- max(sim_a$Cc)
peak_a_brain <- max(sim_a$Cbrain)
end_b <- sim_b[sim_b$time == 65, ]
fig_check <- tibble::tibble(
  quantity = c(
    "Fig 4A: peak blood after bolus (ug/mL)",
    "Fig 3A: peak brain after bolus (ug/g)",
    "Fig 4B: blood at end of 1-h infusion (ug/mL)",
    "Fig 3B: brain at end of 1-h infusion (ug/g)"
  ),
  figure = c(39, 13, 40, 23),
  model = c(peak_a_blood, peak_a_brain, end_b$Cc, end_b$Cbrain)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (model / figure - 1))
knitr::kable(fig_check, digits = 1)
stopifnot(all(abs(fig_check$pct_diff) < 10))
```

## Figure 5: brain target-controlled infusion

The TCI below re-implements the authors' algorithm (`NextStep()` in
`TCIMaster2.m`, after Shafer and Gregg): the infusion rate is constant over
10 s steps; the brain response to one unit step is pre-computed; and at each
step the rate is chosen, by iterating on the time of the resulting brain peak,
so that the predicted peak brain concentration after that step equals the
target. The schedule is then solved through the packaged model as an
independent check that the brain concentration is held at the target.

```{r tci-kernel}
dT <- 10 / 60 # min, TCI step
grid_step <- 1 / 60 # min, 1-s resolution as in the authors' code
horizon <- 90 # min
tgrid <- seq(0, horizon, by = grid_step)

# Brain response to 1 mg/kg/min for one 10-s step.
kernel <- solve_typical(make_events(0, 1, dT, tgrid))$Cbrain
ce_peak <- max(kernel)
tpeak <- which.max(kernel)

tci_schedule <- function(target, n_steps, tol = 0.01) {
  n <- length(tgrid)
  steps_per <- round(dT / grid_step)
  pred <- numeric(n)
  rate <- numeric(n_steps)
  for (s in seq_len(n_steps)) {
    i0 <- (s - 1) * steps_per + 1
    idx <- i0:n
    k <- kernel[seq_along(idx)]
    tp <- tpeak
    for (iter in 1:50) {
      base_at <- pred[min(n, i0 + tp - 1)]
      guess <- max(0, (target - base_at) / ce_peak)
      trial <- pred[idx] + guess * k
      pk <- max(trial)
      tp <- which.max(trial)
      if (guess == 0 || abs(pk - target) / target <= tol) break
    }
    rate[s] <- guess
    pred[idx] <- pred[idx] + guess * k
  }
  tibble::tibble(start = (seq_len(n_steps) - 1) * dT, rate_mgkgmin = rate)
}
```

```{r tci-solve}
tci_duration <- 75 # min, as in Fig 5A/5B
tci_obs <- seq(0, tci_duration, by = 0.1)
run_tci <- function(target) {
  sched <- tci_schedule(target, n_steps = round(tci_duration / dT))
  ev <- make_events(sched$start, sched$rate_mgkgmin, dT, tci_obs)
  ev <- ev[!(ev$evid == 1 & ev$amt == 0), ]
  list(
    schedule = sched |> dplyr::mutate(target = target),
    sim = solve_typical(ev) |> dplyr::mutate(target = target)
  )
}
tci <- lapply(c(10, 15), run_tci)
tci_sched <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(tci, `[[`, "schedule"))
tci_sim <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(tci, `[[`, "sim"))
```

```{r fig-5, fig.height = 6}
p_conc <- tci_sim |>
  dplyr::select(target, time, Blood = Cc, Brain = Cbrain) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Blood, Brain), names_to = "matrix", values_to = "conc") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, conc, colour = matrix)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = target), linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~ paste("Brain target", target, "ug/g")) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Blood = "darkred", Brain = "black")) +
  labs(x = "Time (min)", y = "Propofol (ug/mL blood, ug/g brain)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
p_rate <- tci_sched |>
  ggplot(aes(start, rate_mgkgmin)) +
  geom_step(colour = "grey40") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~ paste("Brain target", target, "ug/g")) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (min)", y = "Infusion rate (mg/kg/min)",
    caption = "Replicates the model lines and infusion profiles of Figure 5A-C of Shortal 2018."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
p_conc
p_rate
```

While the brain concentration is held constant, `d/dt(brain) = 0` forces the
blood concentration to `target * k21 / k12` (17.5 ug/mL for a 10 ug/g target,
the plateau of the red line in Figure 5B). After the first minutes the brain
stays within the algorithm's tolerance of the target, as in Figure 5A/5C. The
maintenance rate at the end of the hour is read from the grey area of Figure
5A/5C (log axis) at about 0.6 and 0.8 mg/kg/min.

```{r fig-5-check}
tci_summary <- tci_sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= 5) |>
  dplyr::group_by(target) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    max_brain_dev_pct = 100 * max(abs(Cbrain / target - 1)),
    blood_end = Cc[time == max(time)],
    blood_expected = target[1] * 2.71 / 1.55,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    tci_sched |>
      dplyr::group_by(target) |>
      dplyr::summarise(rate_last_5min = mean(rate_mgkgmin[start >= tci_duration - 5])),
    by = "target"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(rate_fig5 = c(0.6, 0.8))
knitr::kable(tci_summary, digits = 2)
stopifnot(
  # The algorithm targets the post-step brain peak to 1 percent; between
  # peaks the brain dips by a few percent at most.
  all(tci_summary$max_brain_dev_pct < 5),
  all(abs(tci_summary$blood_end / tci_summary$blood_expected - 1) < 0.05),
  # Read from a log-scale raster axis; only the magnitude is checked.
  all(abs(tci_summary$rate_last_5min / tci_summary$rate_fig5 - 1) < 0.3)
)
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no NCA table. Because the model is linear and drug leaves
only from blood, two exact identities hold for any input and serve as the
check: the blood AUC from zero to infinity equals `dose / (sinf * k10)`, and,
because brain exchanges only with blood, `k12 * AUC_blood = k21 * AUC_brain`.
The terminal half-life equals `log(2)` over the smallest eigenvalue of the
rate matrix in Eq 1. NCA is run per paradigm for both blood and brain, after
a long washout so that the extrapolated fraction is small.

```{r pknca}
obs_nca <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 10, by = 0.05), seq(10, 3000, by = 5))))
nca_sim <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  solve_typical(make_events(0, 150, 0.1, obs_nca)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(treatment = "15 mg/kg bolus", dose_mgkg = 15),
  solve_typical(make_events(0, 2, 60, obs_nca)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(treatment = "2 mg/kg/min x 60 min", dose_mgkg = 120)
)
stopifnot(all(nca_sim$Cc >= -1e-6 * max(nca_sim$Cc)))

nca_long <- nca_sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, treatment, Cc, Cbrain) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Cc, Cbrain), names_to = "matrix", values_to = "conc") |>
  dplyr::mutate(conc = pmax(conc, 0))

doses <- tibble::tibble(
  id = 1L, time = 0,
  treatment = rep(c("15 mg/kg bolus", "2 mg/kg/min x 60 min"), each = 2),
  matrix = rep(c("Cc", "Cbrain"), 2),
  amt = rep(c(15, 120), each = 2) * wt
)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_long, conc ~ time | treatment + matrix + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(doses, amt ~ time | treatment + matrix + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
  aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_tab <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, matrix, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
nca_tab |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Paradigm" = treatment, "Matrix" = matrix,
    "Cmax" = cmax, "Tmax (min)" = tmax,
    "AUC0-inf (obs, ug*min/mL)" = aucinf.obs, "t1/2 (min)" = half.life
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

```{r pknca-identities}
k <- c(k12 = 1.55, k21 = 2.71, k13 = 0.22, k31 = 0.04, k10 = 0.07)
sinf <- 0.35
rate_matrix <- rbind(
  c(-(k[["k12"]] + k[["k13"]] + k[["k10"]]), k[["k21"]], k[["k31"]]),
  c(k[["k12"]], -k[["k21"]], 0),
  c(k[["k13"]], 0, -k[["k31"]])
)
t_half_terminal <- log(2) / min(abs(eigen(rate_matrix)$values))

identities <- nca_tab |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    dose_mgkg = ifelse(treatment == "15 mg/kg bolus", 15, 120),
    auc_expected = dose_mgkg / (sinf * k[["k10"]]) *
      ifelse(matrix == "Cbrain", k[["k12"]] / k[["k21"]], 1),
    auc_pct_diff = 100 * (aucinf.obs / auc_expected - 1),
    thalf_expected = t_half_terminal,
    thalf_pct_diff = 100 * (half.life / thalf_expected - 1)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, matrix, aucinf.obs, auc_expected, auc_pct_diff,
                half.life, thalf_expected, thalf_pct_diff)
knitr::kable(identities, digits = 2)
stopifnot(
  # Trapezoidal AUC on a 5-min tail grid after a 0.05-min early grid:
  # measured within about 1 percent of the closed form.
  all(abs(identities$auc_pct_diff) < 2),
  all(abs(identities$thalf_pct_diff) < 2)
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **No variability model.** The paper fitted the constants by unweighted
  least squares on all blood and brain concentrations (Methods, 'Fitting
  procedure') and reports no between-animal or residual variance. The model
  therefore has no etas, and the additive residual SDs for blood and brain
  are `fixed(0)` placeholders; simulations are deterministic.
* **Concentration-scale states.** Eq 1 is written for the concentrations
  `x1`, `x2`, `x3` with input `I(t) / sinf`. The packaged ODEs multiply every
  equation by `vc = sinf * WT`, so each state equals its paper concentration
  times `vc`, and `Cbrain = brain / vc`. The brain state is therefore a scaled
  quantity, not the physical amount of propofol in the brain: the paper's
  rate constants are defined on concentrations and do not identify a brain
  volume.
* **Body weight.** Because the input is in mg/kg/min and the blood volume is
  `sinf` per kg, body weight cancels from every concentration. `WT` is kept
  so doses can be given in mg; simulations use the study mean of 0.0274 kg.
* **Units.** Time is in min, doses in mg and concentrations in mg/L, which
  equals ug/mL. Blood concentrations are in ug/mL and brain concentrations in
  ug/g; the model treats 1 mL of blood and 1 g of brain alike, as the paper
  does when it fits both with the same equations and plots both in ug/g.
* **Table 1 versus the authors' code.** The final constants in the authors'
  TCI code agree with Table 1 to its two-decimal rounding (table above).
  The packaged model uses Table 1; the larger relative rounding is on `k31`
  (0.04 vs 0.042 1/min) and `k10` (0.07 vs 0.072 1/min).
* **TCI re-implementation.** The TCI in this article follows the logic of the
  authors' `NextStep()` function with a 10-s step and a 1 percent tolerance,
  using the packaged model for the impulse response. It is a check of the
  model, not a port of the pump-control software.
* **Figure values.** The comparison values for Figures 3, 4 and 5 were read by
  the maintainers from the published raster figures.
* **Errata.** No correction notice for this article was found in Europe PMC
  as of 2026-11-25.
